title: AI Model Analysis
description: Generate AI critiques that explain policy models in plain language (executive summary, strengths, weaknesses, hidden trade-offs, implementation risks, socio-economic impacts, alternatives) while keeping scoring strictly deterministic. AI interprets; it never scores.
rationale: AI commentary makes models accessible to non-experts, surfaces non-obvious trade-offs, and adds qualitative depth on top of the quantitative scores - without compromising the reproducibility guarantee.
success_criteria: For a saved model, the AI produces all seven critique sections
Critique is grounded in the model's actual inputs, outputs and scores
The deterministic score is unchanged by, and shown independently of, the AI
notes:
## Scope (in)
- Critique outputs: executive summary, strengths, weaknesses, hidden trade-offs, implementation risks, socio-economic impacts, alternative recommendations

## Out of scope
- Any AI influence on scores (EPIC-003 stays deterministic)
- The provider framework (EPIC-008) and user keys (EPIC-009)

## Dependencies
- EPIC-003 - AI is given the deterministic scores + rationale to explain
- EPIC-004 - analysis runs against a saved model
- EPIC-008 - analysis calls go through the provider framework

## Assumptions
- AI receives model inputs, engine outputs and scores as grounding context
- Outputs are advisory commentary, clearly labelled AI-generated
- The same deterministic score is shown regardless of which AI is used

## Risks
- AI appears to set the score -> hard separation; UI states 'AI explains, not scores'
- Hallucinated facts -> ground prompts in actual model data; label as AI opinion
- Inconsistent output structure -> structured prompt templates + output schema
- Sensitive/biased commentary -> neutral prompting; disclaimers; dismissable

## Future extensions
- Comparative critique across two models
- Critique in multiple tones/audiences (policymaker vs citizen)
- Feeding alternative recommendations back as suggested slider changes
